steps.say: The skull is a rigid box with three tenants. When a fourth arrives as blood or swelling, something has to give, and that something is the brain.
steps.tx: The **Monro-Kellie doctrine** (fixed vault rule) states that blood, brain and **cerebrospinal fluid** (brain water) share a fixed skull volume, so any new mass first displaces fluid and venous blood and then raises **intracranial pressure** (brain pressure) steeply once compensation is exhausted and compliance is lost across the three **intracranial compartments** (vault divisions).

steps.say: Twenty two is the number that triggers treatment. Sustained pressure above it independently predicts death after severe injury.
steps.tx: Brain Trauma Foundation guidance treats sustained **intracranial pressure** (brain pressure) above **22 mmHg** (twenty two pressure units) because values beyond this threshold independently predict death and poor recovery after **severe brain injury** (coma producing trauma), and the figure is written into every ICU protocol chart as the **22 mmHg threshold** (treatment trigger).

steps.say: Pressure means nothing without blood flow behind it. Perfusion pressure is the difference between arterial inflow and intracranial resistance.
steps.tx: **Cerebral perfusion pressure** (brain blood push) is held at **60 to 70 mmHg** (sixty to seventy pressure units), avoiding below **50 mmHg** (fifty units) where **ischaemia** (brain starvation) begins, and prolonged above 70 with aggressive fluids and **pressors** (pressure drugs) since lung injury and swelling worsen outcome.

steps.say: Start with the simple measures before any drugs. Position, sedation and fever control fix half of all pressure spikes.
steps.tx: First-tier measures are **30 degree head elevation** (bed head raised) with a neutral neck, adequate analgesia and **propofol sedation** (sleep drug), fever control, seizure control and fluid drainage through a **ventricular catheter** (brain water tube), which both monitors pressure and treats it directly.

steps.say: Salt water pulls water out of the swollen brain. Hypertonic saline suits low pressure patients while mannitol needs good kidneys and pressure.
steps.tx: **Hyperosmolar therapy** (salt water treatment) uses **3 percent hypertonic saline** (strong salt water) boluses or **mannitol** (sugar water drug) **0.25 to 1 g per kg** (quarter to one gram per kilo), preferring saline when systolic pressure is borderline, given as **250 mL** (two fifty millilitre) boluses, and watching serum sodium and osmolarity ceilings with repeated blood tests.

steps.say: Blowing off carbon dioxide shrinks brain vessels fast. It buys minutes for theatre, but routine use starves the injured brain.
steps.tx: Brief **hyperventilation** (fast breathing) to a **carbon dioxide** (blood gas) of **30 to 35** (thirty to thirty five) is only a bridge to definitive evacuation, and prophylactic hyperventilation below that range in the first **24 hours** (first day) is forbidden because it causes **ischaemia** (brain starvation).

steps.say: When everything else fails, coma drugs and cold used to be next. Trials reshaped this ladder, so know what fell off it.
steps.tx: High-dose **barbiturates** (coma drugs) with burst-suppression monitoring control refractory pressure but drop blood pressure and immunity, **CRASH steroids** (harmful steroid use) worsen death, and prophylactic **hypothermia** (cooling) is not routine after the Eurotherm trial showed harm in closed injury cohorts.

steps.say: Pressure control fails without body care. Feeding, clot prevention and waking the patient daily complete the bundle.
steps.tx: Early **enteral nutrition** (gut feeding) within **72 hours** (three days), chemical **DVT prophylaxis** (clot prevention) once the CT is stable, and daily awakening with **delirium screening** (confusion check) complete the **ICU bundle** (combined care set) around pressure control for every severe injury admission.
